title: Knee Pain & Osteoarthritis (Sandhivata): Ayurvedic Causes, Diet, Exercise & Care
excerpt: Knee pain while climbing stairs, a cracking sound when getting up or sitting down, and morning stiffness — these are common signs of knee osteoarthritis (Sandhivata). Learn how Ayurveda understands Sandhivata — causes, symptoms, tests, what to eat and avoid, exercise, safe home remedies and when you must see a doctor immediately.
content:
As age increases, many people start having knee pain — difficulty climbing or coming down stairs, trouble getting up after sitting on the floor, stiffness when walking after sitting for a long time, and a cracking sound from the knee.

In Ayurveda this wear-and-tear knee pain is called Sandhivata (Janu Sandhivata). The good news is that with the right diet, weight control, regular exercise and proper care, most people can reduce pain and do their daily work comfortably. This article is for information only — take treatment only on the advice of your Vaidya or doctor.

What is knee osteoarthritis (Sandhivata)?

The knee joint is formed where the thigh bone and the shin bone meet. The ends of these bones are covered with a smooth, cushioning layer called cartilage, and there is a lubricating fluid inside the joint. Together they let the knee bend and straighten without friction.

Because of age, extra weight, an old injury or excessive strain, this cartilage slowly wears away and becomes thin. The bones then start rubbing against each other, causing pain, stiffness, swelling and difficulty in walking. This is called osteoarthritis (OA).

The Ayurvedic view: Sandhivata

According to Ayurveda, Sandhivata is a disease caused by aggravated Vata dosha (a Vatavyadhi). With age, Vata naturally increases and the nourishment of Asthi (bone) and Sandhi (joints) starts to decrease. Charaka Samhita describes the sign of Vata lodged in the joints as follows:

वातपूर्णदृतिस्पर्शः शोथः सन्धिगतेऽनिले ।
प्रसारणाकुञ्चनयोः प्रवृत्तिश्च सवेदना ॥
— Charaka Samhita, Chikitsa Sthana 28 (Vatavyadhi Chikitsa)

Meaning: When Vata settles in a joint, there is a swelling which, on touch, feels like a leather bag filled with air, and there is pain while extending (straightening) and flexing (bending) the joint.

That is why the basic principle of Sandhivata care in Ayurveda is — calming Vata (snehana, i.e. oil and ghee, and swedana, i.e. warm fomentation), keeping Agni healthy so that ama (undigested toxic residue) is not formed, and nourishing the dhatus. Note that if the joint is red and hot and many joints are swollen, it may be Amavata or another disease, which is treated differently.

Main causes

  • Increasing age (especially after 45–50 years) and, in women, after menopause
  • Excess weight or obesity — constant extra load on the knees
  • An old knee injury, ligament or meniscus injury
  • Standing for very long, climbing stairs repeatedly, lifting heavy weights
  • Lack of exercise and weak thigh muscles
  • Dry, cold, stale and too little food; staying hungry for long
  • Deficiency of vitamin D and calcium, not going out in the sun
  • Someone in the family having this problem

Symptoms

  • Knee pain while walking, climbing or coming down stairs, or getting up and sitting down
  • Stiffness on waking in the morning or after sitting for long (usually less than half an hour)
  • A cracking or grinding sound when bending or straightening the knee
  • Mild swelling around the knee
  • The knee not bending fully or not straightening fully
  • Pain increasing after walking for long and reducing with rest
  • In advanced stages, bowing of the legs and limping

Remember — if there is swelling in many joints (such as the finger joints), morning stiffness lasts more than an hour, or there is sudden severe pain and redness in the big toe, it may be rheumatoid arthritis or gout. Their tests and treatment are different.

Tests

If needed, the doctor may advise these tests:

  • X-ray (taken standing) — shows narrowing of the joint space and wear of the bone
  • Blood tests — such as ESR/CRP, RA factor and uric acid, to rule out other types of arthritis
  • Vitamin D, calcium and, if needed, MRI (in case of injury or ligament problems)

Diet: what to eat, what to avoid

In Sandhivata, food that calms Vata is beneficial — that is, warm, fresh, slightly unctuous (with ghee or oil) and easy to digest.

What to eat

  • Grains: wheat, old rice, bajra (pearl millet, in winter), daliya (broken wheat)
  • Pulses: moong, masoor, arhar (toor) — well cooked, tempered with hing and cumin
  • Vegetables: bottle gourd, ridge gourd, pointed gourd (parwal), pumpkin, carrot, beetroot, spinach, drumstick (moringa) pods
  • Milk and ghee: warm milk (with turmeric), a little desi ghee in food
  • Seeds and nuts: sesame, flaxseed, soaked almonds, walnuts — in small amounts
  • Spices: dry ginger (sonth), turmeric, fenugreek, ajwain, garlic — in normal amounts in food
  • Lukewarm water; 15–20 minutes of morning sunlight daily

What to avoid or greatly reduce

  • Cold, refrigerated, stale and dry food
  • Too much chana, rajma, peas and raw salad (Vata-increasing, especially at night)
  • Maida, bakery items, junk food, too much sugar and cold drinks
  • Very fried food and too much salt
  • Late-night meals and frequent fasting or staying hungry for long
  • Alcohol and smoking

Weight control

While walking, the knees bear pressure many times greater than body weight, so even a small loss of weight can reduce knee pain considerably.

Daily routine and knee care

  • Do some light activity every morning; do not sit in one position for too long
  • Minimise sitting cross-legged on the floor, squatting and using Indian-style toilets — use a chair and a western-style toilet
  • Climb fewer stairs; hold the railing while climbing
  • Wear comfortable shoes with cushioned soles; do not wear high heels
  • If pain is severe, use a walking stick (in the hand opposite to the painful knee) or a knee cap for support
  • Protect the knees from cold wind and cold floors, especially in winter
  • Sleep on time at night

Exercise, yoga and pranayama

  • Muscle-strengthening exercises: lying down and lifting the straight leg (straight leg raise), pressing a towel placed under the knee (quadriceps setting), straightening the leg while sitting on a chair
  • Asanas: Tadasana, Vrikshasana (with support), Setu Bandhasana, Pawanmuktasana, Shavasana
  • Pranayama: Anulom-Vilom, Bhramari

Start exercise slowly and learn it from a trained yoga teacher or physiotherapist. Do not do Vajrasana, Padmasana, deep squats or jerky exercises when you have knee pain. If there is fresh swelling, injury or an operation on the knee, or you have heart disease/high BP, ask your Vaidya/doctor first.

Safe home remedies

  • Oil massage (abhyanga): warm sesame oil and massage the knees gently for 10–15 minutes
  • Fomentation (swedana): after the massage, apply a hot-water bag or warm towel for 10–15 minutes
  • Turmeric milk: a little turmeric in warm milk at night
  • Fenugreek (methi): use fenugreek seeds or fenugreek leaves in food
  • Dry ginger (sonth): a little dry ginger or fresh ginger in dal and vegetables

If the knee suddenly becomes red, hot and badly swollen, do not do oil massage or hot fomentation — first see a Vaidya/doctor. People taking blood-thinning medicines should ask their doctor before taking extra turmeric or fenugreek.

Ayurvedic herbs — with caution

Ayurvedic texts and some modern studies mention several medicines for Sandhivata, such as Shallaki (Boswellia), Guggulu (classical formulations like Yogaraj Guggulu), Ashwagandha, Rasna, Nirgundi, Dashamoola and Haridra (turmeric). However:

  • Which medicine, in what dose and for how long — the Vaidya decides this only after looking at each person's prakriti, pulse, age, digestion and stage of the disease.
  • Guggulu-based medicines are not suitable in pregnancy and with some medicines; do not take them for long on your own.
  • Do not stop your ongoing medicines (BP, sugar, blood thinners, thyroid, etc.) on your own. Do not take painkillers for a long time without a doctor's advice — they can harm the stomach and kidneys.
  • In pregnancy, breastfeeding, children and the very elderly, give any medicine only on the advice of a Vaidya/doctor. Beware of claims like “knee pain removed from the root” or “you will never need an operation”.

When to see a doctor immediately

  • Sudden severe swelling, redness and warmth in the knee — especially with fever
  • Being unable to put weight on the knee after an injury, the knee getting stuck (locking) or repeatedly giving way
  • Sudden swelling, pain and warmth in the calf
  • Severe pain even at rest at night, unexplained weight loss or fever
  • The leg bending rapidly or walking almost stopping
  • Swelling in many joints together and morning stiffness lasting more than an hour

Summary — points to remember

  • Keep your weight under control — this is the biggest relief for the knees
  • Warm, fresh food with a little ghee; reduce cold, stale and junk food
  • Daily light exercise and exercises that strengthen the thigh muscles
  • Avoid squatting or sitting cross-legged; warm oil massage and fomentation
  • Do not stop ongoing medicines on your own; Ayurvedic treatment only on the advice of an experienced Vaidya
